title: The Placement Test
primary_metric: statistically attributable conversions per dollar of ad spend, comparing the single-placement plan against the full permutation-space multi-variant test

options.A: The Straight Cut — a single fixed placement: the product mention airs at one fixed point in the sponsored video, with one call-to-action style, for the whole campaign window
options.B: The Full Rotation — a full multi-variant test cycling through all three placement-timing video cuts (Early/Mid/Late mention) combined with two call-to-action styles, six distinct variants in total

sources.claim: Google Ads' recommended minimum conversion volume for a statistically reliable Smart Bidding performance read
sources.units: conversions per 30-day period (50 for Target ROAS)
sources.title: About Smart Bidding — Google Ads Help
sources.note: Re-sourced 2026-08-27 (P6 data-decay fix): the case's prior primary URL (support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6268633, 'Tips on measuring Smart Bidding performance') no longer visibly carries the cited figure on repeated live fetch -- it now shows an unrelated '50 conversions' mention unrelated to this claim. This URL was previously the corroborating citation and was re-verified live on 2026-08-27 to carry the figure verbatim: 'Google Ads recommends measuring performance over longer time periods that have at least 30 conversions, such as a month or longer (50 conversions for Target ROAS).' Promoted to primary citation; the old primary URL is dropped rather than kept as a secondary reference, since it no longer supports the claim. Graded MEDIUM rather than HIGH because Google's help pages carry no explicit publication or last-updated date, even though this is a primary source directly fetched.

sources.claim: Meta's stated minimum optimization-event volume for an ad set to exit the Learning phase
sources.title: About learning limited — Meta Business Help Center
sources.note: Meta's own page states: 'An ad set becomes Learning limited when it is unlikely to receive around 50 optimisation events in the week after your last significant edit.' Confirmed via two independent search-result snippets quoting the page verbatim, but WebFetch could not retrieve the page body directly (Meta Business Help Center serves a JS-rendered shell to the fetch tool — a tooling limitation, not evidence against the figure). Graded MEDIUM for that verification gap plus the missing publication date.

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Jaylen Ortiz, Social Media/Influencer Marketing Strategist, mid-size direct-to-consumer brand

deliverables.text: A permutation calculation, shown with the formula and every step, for the number of distinct possible production-order sequences in which the three placement-timing video cuts could be produced across the production weeks remaining before quarter-end.
A budget-per-variant table comparing The Straight Cut's single-variant budget to The Full Rotation's six-variant budget split, in dollars per variant, with the arithmetic shown.
A minimum-viable-spend clearance table showing, for each plan, what percent of the ad platform's minimum recommended per-variant spend threshold each variant's budget actually represents.

A final recommendation table reporting statistically attributable conversions per dollar of ad spend for The Straight Cut and for The Full Rotation, with a recommendation stated and defended using that number.

balance.argument_a: The Straight Cut puts the entire $60,000 fixed test budget behind 1 variant, 6x more spend per variant than Option B's $10,000 split and well above the $5,000/variant minimum-viable-spend threshold in Appendix C, so its conversion-rate read is the single most statistically reliable number this campaign can produce this quarter — but it only ever tests 1 of the 6 possible placement-timing/CTA combinations, so it can prove that one combination works without ever revealing whether a different combination would have worked better.
balance.argument_b: The Full Rotation tests all 6 placement-timing/CTA combinations at once, splitting the identical $60,000 budget into 6 variants at $10,000 each, so it is the only plan that can actually tell Jaylen which lever (timing, CTA style, or their interaction) drives conversion — and, at this budget, all 6 of those $10,000 splits clear the $5,000/variant Appendix C threshold with real room to spare (double the minimum, not exactly at it), so none of the extra signal The Full Rotation was built to capture gets thrown out as statistically unusable.
balance.margin_basis: Once Appendices B, C and D are sourced, compare statistically attributable conversions per dollar of ad spend for The Straight Cut (1 variant at full budget, benchmarked against Appendix D's conversion-rate and CPM ranges) against The Full Rotation (6 variants at one-sixth budget each, with any variant that fails to clear Appendix C's minimum-spend threshold flagged as non-statistically-usable and excluded from B's attributable-conversions total, not silently counted at face value).
balance.margin_note: RECORDED HONESTLY, ARITHMETIC COMPLETED -- not a fabricated number. At the case's originally stated $18,000 budget, margin_basis's own exclusion rule dropped all six Full Rotation variants ($3,000/variant < Appendix C's $5,000/variant threshold), leaving Option B with zero usable attributable conversions -- a real SPEC §2 balance failure. First fixed by raising MA2 to $30,000, the exact flip threshold the case's own MA2 sensitivity note documented, producing an exact tie -- but at ZERO SLACK: B's $5,000/variant spend equaled the threshold precisely, so P5's ±50% flex sweep later confirmed three independently plausible moves (MA1 up, MA2 down, MA3 up) each flipped ALL SIX Full Rotation variants below threshold SIMULTANEOUSLY (every variant gets an identical split spend, so they cross the line together, not gradually), handing Option A a ~100%-margin win. 2026-08-30 SECOND RETUNE, to give the tie genuine slack instead of a bigger cliff: MA2 raised again, $30,000 -> $60,000. Grounding: $60,000/quarter is a defensible paid-social test budget for a mid-size direct-to-consumer brand's single sponsored-video campaign cycle -- Background frames this as a locked quarterly line item, and doubling the prior figure keeps it in the same order of magnitude the case already established rather than inventing a new scale. At $60,000, Full Rotation's split is $10,000/variant -- double the $5,000/variant Appendix C threshold, not exactly equal to it. Because MA4/MA5 apply identically to both options once every variant clears, conversions-per-dollar is still a rate independent of the split, so the tie is preserved exactly (1000/CPM x conversion_rate = 1.333333 conversions/$, i.e. 80,000 total conversions each on the full $60,000 spend; margin_pct = 0.0%). VERIFIED GENUINE SLACK, not just a bigger cliff: re-running sensitivity_model.py's ±50% flex sweep on all five stated assumption dials at the new $60,000 baseline shows ZERO of the ten flex directions flips the recommendation -- including total_budget's own -50% flex, which lands exactly back on the old $30,000 boundary and still clears (does not fall below). The worst single-dial move (weeks_remaining or cost_per_conversion at +50%) raises the per-variant threshold to $7,500, which the $10,000/variant split clears with $2,500 (33%) to spare. tier2_probes.py --probe 5 --flex 0.5 confirms this mechanically: PASS, 0 of 10 flex directions flip or breach the 20% cap. The real tension the tie exposes is now purely qualitative -- Argument A's single-hypothesis reliability versus Argument B's genuine multi-variant signal -- which the quantitative primary metric alone cannot settle, but which is no longer confounded by a knife-edge arithmetic accident. Full arithmetic in FACILITATOR.md's Facilitator-only numbers section and case.json.derived.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Detail internal to Jaylen's fictional employer's production calendar; no public source can exist for it. Set greater than the 3 required cuts so the D1 permutation calculation requires the full nPr formula rather than a trivial 3!.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Changes the magnitude of D1's permutation count, and is also a factor in the Appendix C threshold formula's week-count term (50 events/week [S2] x weeks_remaining x $20/conversion [MA3]). At the current 5 weeks, the threshold is $5,000/variant. Raising weeks_remaining raises that threshold directly -- at 7.5 weeks (a +50% move) the threshold rises to $7,500/variant. 2026-08-30 retune (MA2 raised to $60,000, $10,000/variant): this +50% move on MA1 no longer flips the recommendation -- Full Rotation's $10,000/variant split still clears the raised $7,500/variant threshold, with $2,500 (33%) to spare. (Before the retune, at the original $30,000 budget, this same move did flip the recommendation to Option A; see case.json.balance.margin_note for the full retune history.)

modeling_assumptions.placeholder_location: Appendix B, total fixed ad-spend budget
modeling_assumptions.assumption: Total fixed ad-spend budget for the quarter's test
modeling_assumptions.basis: Detail internal to Jaylen's fictional employer's already-locked budget; unsourceable by construction. Divides evenly by 6 variants ($10,000/variant) for clean D2 arithmetic. Originally set to $18,000 (a genuine SPEC §2 balance failure), then $30,000 (the exact point where every Full Rotation variant's split spend cleared Appendix C's $5,000/variant threshold, but with zero slack), then raised again 2026-08-30 to $60,000 specifically to give the tie real robustness -- see case.json.balance.margin_note for the full retune history and the $60,000/quarter grounding.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Load-bearing for D3/D4, but now with genuine slack. Full Rotation's $10,000/variant split is double the $5,000/variant Appendix C threshold. sensitivity_model.py's ±50% flex sweep (2026-08-30, post-retune) confirms 0 of 10 flex directions across all five stated dials (including this one's own -50% flex, which lands exactly on the old $30,000 boundary and still clears) flips the recommendation -- the worst case (weeks_remaining or cost_per_conversion at +50%) still clears the raised $7,500/variant threshold with $2,500 (33%) to spare. Below roughly $30,000 total (a -50%+ move well past the tested ±50% band), one or more Full Rotation variants would fall short and be excluded, reducing or zeroing Option B's D4 figure -- that boundary still exists, it is just no longer within a single ±50% assumption swing.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Assumed average cost per attributable conversion
modeling_assumptions.basis: Neither Meta nor Google publishes an official dollar minimum-spend threshold, only conversion-count thresholds (S1, S2). Converting the sourced conversion-count threshold to dollars for Challenge D3 requires this estimate. Public per-conversion cost figures found ranged roughly $2-$60 across non-primary sources with no single authoritative figure freely available; $20 is a round mid-range figure for clean classroom arithmetic, not a cited statistic.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Raising this raises the Appendix C dollar threshold. At the current $60,000 budget ($10,000/variant), Full Rotation clears the threshold even at a +50% move (cost_per_conversion at $30/conversion raises the threshold to $7,500/variant, still $2,500 below the $10,000 split) -- sensitivity_model.py's ±50% flex confirms this does not flip D4. (Before the 2026-08-30 retune, at the original $30,000 budget, any increase above $20/conversion did flip the recommendation; see case.json.balance.margin_note.)

modeling_assumptions.placeholder_location: Appendix D, industry benchmark conversion rate range
modeling_assumptions.assumption: Industry benchmark conversion rate used in D4
modeling_assumptions.basis: Contested figure: search results ranged from under 1% to over 14% depending on site/funnel/industry with no shared primary source; IAB publishes no free point figure and eMarketer's benchmark data is subscription-gated (confirmed via direct fetch returning 404 on the free page). 2% stated as a reasonable typical value, not a cited fact.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Applies identically to both options in the D4 conversions-per-dollar calculation, so it does not by itself flip the recommendation — that flip is driven by MA2/MA3.

modeling_assumptions.placeholder_location: Appendix D, industry benchmark CPM range
modeling_assumptions.assumption: Industry benchmark CPM used in D4
modeling_assumptions.basis: Same contested-figure situation as MA4: found CPM figures ranged roughly $7-$30+ across non-primary aggregator sources with no authoritative convergence, and eMarketer's paid data was not accessible. $15 stated as a reasonable typical value, not a cited fact.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Applies identically to both options; does not independently flip the recommendation.

sensitivity_note: MA2 (total ad-spend budget, now $60,000 after the 2026-08-30 retune) is the load-bearing figure for whether Full Rotation's variants clear the Appendix C $5,000/variant threshold: below $30,000 total (a -50%+ move), one or more variants fail to clear and D4's comparison degrades or fully favors Option A; at or above $30,000, every variant clears and, because MA4/MA5 (conversion rate, CPM) apply identically to both options, D4 ties exactly at 0.0% margin. Unlike the case's prior $30,000 setting (which sat exactly at that boundary with zero slack), $60,000 gives real headroom: Full Rotation's $10,000/variant split is double the base $5,000/variant threshold. sensitivity_model.py's ±50% flex sweep confirms 0 of 10 flex directions across all five stated dials (weeks_remaining, total_budget, cost_per_conversion, conversion_rate, cpm) flips the recommendation or breaches the 20% cap -- including total_budget's own -50% flex, which lands exactly on the old $30,000 boundary and still clears. MA1 and MA3 both still affect the Appendix C threshold formula (50 events/week x weeks_remaining x cost_per_conversion), so they remain load-bearing in principle, but at the new budget their worst-case +50% move only raises the threshold to $7,500/variant, which the $10,000/variant split clears with $2,500 (33%) to spare. MA4 and MA5 affect D4's magnitude identically for both options and do not independently flip the recommendation.

derived.d1_permutations: P(5,3) = 5 x 4 x 3 = 60 distinct production-order sequences

d3_threshold_clearance_pct.full_rotation: $10,000 / $5,000 x 100 = 200% (clears with real room to spare -- double the threshold, not exactly at it)

d4_conversions_per_dollar.straight_cut_total_conversions: $60,000 x 1.333333 = 80,000 (all attributable -- the one variant clears)
d4_conversions_per_dollar.full_rotation_total_conversions: 6 x ($10,000 x 1.333333) = 6 x 13,333.33 = 80,000 (all attributable -- all six variants clear)
